title: Dissection and tissue studies; PCR and gel electrophoresis

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Vein
items.clue: Vessel with a thin wall that collapses flat.

items.label: Artery
items.clue: Vessel with a thick, elastic wall that stays open.

items.label: DNA ladder
items.clue: Set of fragments of known length, run in one lane for comparison.

items.label: PCR
items.clue: Tube technique that copies one chosen stretch of DNA, doubling the target in every cycle.

questions.stem: Why is Taq polymerase, rather than a DNA polymerase from human cells, used in the polymerase chain reaction?

options.text: It is not denatured at the high temperature used to separate the strands, so it lasts through every cycle.
It is a bacterial enzyme that copies DNA much faster than a human polymerase, so fewer cycles are needed.
It separates the two strands of the template by itself, so no helicase has to be added to the reaction mixture.
It can start a new strand anywhere on a bare template, so no primers are needed in the reaction mixture.

questions.explanation: Each cycle heats the mixture to about 95°C to separate the strands. Taq polymerase, from the hot-spring bacterium Thermus aquaticus, keeps its shape at this temperature, so it does not have to be replaced after each cycle.

questions.stem: A student dissects a set of sheep's lungs. Near the lungs she finds two tubes side by side. Tube P has C-shaped rings of cartilage in its wall and stays open when empty. Tube Q has a thin, soft wall with no cartilage and collapses flat. Which identification do these observations best support?

options.text: P is an artery: it has the thicker wall and stays open, as arteries do.
P is a bronchus, held open by its cartilage; Q is a blood vessel.
Q is an artery: blood at high pressure needs a wide, soft-walled vessel.
Q is a vein, because it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.explanation: Structure identifies it: C-shaped cartilage keeps airways open. A thin wall that collapses fits a vein, such as a pulmonary vein.

questions.stem: A PCR reaction starts with 3 double-stranded DNA molecules of the target section. How many double-stranded molecules of the target are present after 4 complete cycles?
questions.explanation: Every molecule is copied in every cycle, so the number doubles each cycle: 3 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 3 × 2⁴ = 48.

questions.stem: Three DNA fragments of 200, 500 and 1200 base pairs are loaded into the same well of a gel and a voltage is applied. Which statement describes the result?

options.text: The 200 base pair fragment moves furthest through the gel, towards the positive electrode.
The 1200 base pair fragment moves furthest, because it carries the most negative charge and is pulled harder.
The 200 base pair fragment moves furthest, towards the negative electrode at the far end of the gel.
The three fragments separate according to their base sequences rather than by their lengths.
